science of all ages and pertaining to all rational creatuees whether on earth or in Purgatory or in Heaven, not, however, to the atheist or the reprobate, -- the latter hopelessly lost by a choice of his own, the former -- by his own free choice also -- a positive canditate for perdition: "'He that believeth . shall be saved; He that believeth not shall be condemned." Hence the definition:
"Religion: the science of our happy relationship
WITH God and our neighbor."
Incidently, we might add that, like with other sciences, or branches of science, -- though there may be a thousand systems of religion -- there can be but one religion, according to the above.
As to Religion's "would-be-destruction", atheism; It really ought to suffice to know that atheism is positively and diametrically opposed to religion of any kind according to the above definition, and that of whatever system; that it would deprive man -- actually does deprive man in asmuch as it prevails -- of the privileged, the super- naturally hopefully duty of loving God and neighbor; thus aiming at positively hinilizing the very sources and soul of the supernatural and again; thus, by degrading man below the brute-beast that has no faculties for exercising hope, offers him despair instead. Hence the demand for what may seem strong words in the definition:
(unfinished draft)
